fields.v: Xia, H., Wu, E., & Park, Y. (2026). Passes Alone, Fails Together: Benchmarking Semantic Coordination in Parallel LLM-Agent Development. In Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on Explainable and Reliable Software Systems (EXPRESS '26), October 4-9, 2026, Oakland, CA, USA. ACM, 6 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3842650.3843171 (also arXiv:2609.25396v1)
Workshop — EXPRESS '26 (2nd Workshop on Explainable and Reliable Software Systems), ACM; received 2026-06-28, accepted 2026-07-31; 6 pages
Academia: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Columbia University

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — stale, a benchmark for semantic coordination of parallel coding agents (patches that pass alone but fail when merged), with the interference metric Δblind, a deterministic PR-pair mining pipeline and three tiers (synthetic, mined PR pairs, constructed real-derived Django tasks); preliminary study with blind, informed and oracle-message (comm) conditions

No SDD approach. Conditions: solo, blind (parallel agents without seeing each other's change, diffs merged), informed (sequential oracle, sees completed edits), comm (oracle message ~130 tokens describing the completed change). Agents: mini-swe-agent and OpenHands with 'a GPT-5-class coding model' (mined tier); GPT-5.5 (synthetic replication, real-derived tier). Versions: Not stated

Not an approach. Task inputs: task description from the issue/PR (solution text removed), hidden gold test patch; in comm a templated message describing the other worker's completed change (new helper names, required arguments or return types)
N/A. Evaluation flow: agents solve tasks on a shared base commit (solo/blind), patches merged with git, agent test edits discarded, gold tests applied, combined test set run in every condition

Existing code base (Django; mining also on SymPy, xarray, seaborn): pairs of tasks from merged PRs, synthetic wrapper tasks over added helpers, and constructed consumer functions over real Django helpers

Mined: 685 Django PRs -> 4,262 candidate pairs -> 417 validated pairs (834 runs); 30 pairs in other repos (SymPy 11, xarray 12, seaborn 7); 23 disjoint controls. Synthetic: 3 mechanisms x 4 degrees, 8 trials each (96 cells), n=4 helpers. Real-derived: 12 Django helpers x 3 mechanisms = 36 instances, 3 trials each (108 blind + 108 comm runs). More than 4,000 graded task solves in total

Automatic: same combined gold test set run on each patch alone and on the merge, after discarding agent test edits; deterministic pair validation (clean merge, base validity)

Criterion: Δblind on the combined gold test set; no success threshold stated by the authors, so verdicts for all entries: no criterion stated by the authors. (a) Synthetic tier, blind, agent/model not stated in that paragraph (GPT-5.5 replicated it): renames and required-argument changes Δblind = number of changed helpers, zero variance; mean interference 2.50. (b) Synthetic, informed: no failures for renames/arguments; 0.13 failures per run on return-type changes. (c) Synthetic, comm (oracle message ~130 tokens): mean interference 0.04 (98% reduction). (d) Mined Django tier, mini-swe-agent and OpenHands + 'GPT-5-class coding model', solo/blind: 1 of 834 runs with Δblind > 0 (one failing test) after corrected grading. (e) Mined, GPT-5.5 on most strongly coupled pairs: no interference in 72 runs. (f) Real-derived Django tier, GPT-5.5, blind: interference in 105/108 runs (97%), on all 12 helpers. (g) Real-derived, GPT-5.5, comm: 89/108 recovered (82%; 93% among cleanly merging patches; all 36 return-type runs recovered). Cost: not measured

Tasks: synthetic, mined PR pairs and constructed real-derived instances from a shared base commit. Conditions: solo vs blind (same patches reused in the merge, so run differences cannot explain Δblind), informed oracle (synthetic only), comm oracle message (synthetic and real-derived). Constant: model, harness, shared base, combined test set. Baseline: solo patches; informed as ideal-visibility baseline. Acceptance: hidden gold tests. Repetitions: 8 trials per synthetic setting, 3 trials per real-derived instance; mined tier 834 runs on 417 pairs, but the text does not say whether the two runs per pair are the two tasks of the pair, the two harnesses (mini-swe-agent, OpenHands) or repetitions. Human intervention: none
fields.why: Section 4 only says 'Of 834 runs on 417 validated Django pairs' and that the model ran with mini-swe-agent and OpenHands; 834 = 2 x 417 fits the two tasks of each pair (one solve each, reused in blind), but the two harnesses or repetitions are also possible readings.
fields.doubt: 834 runs em 417 pares: o mais provável é uma execução por tarefa (2 por par), mas o artigo não o diz e menciona dois harnesses. Confirma na secção 4 se há repetições no tier minerado.

fields.v: Blind parallel work produced interference on controlled tasks (synthetic: Δblind equals changed interfaces; real-derived: 97%); oracle message reduced synthetic interference by 98% (2.50 -> 0.04) and recovered 82% of real-derived runs; mined reviewed PR pairs showed almost no interference (1/834). Naive grading (different test sets, agent test edits) falsely inflated interference. No significance tests

Partly: corrected grading separated patch-interaction failures from individual failures and distinguished blind vs oracle conditions on controlled tasks, but mined PR history gave almost no interference to measure. Limitations stated by the authors: constructed rates do not estimate real prevalence or severity; experiments limited to Django; scripted breaking patch; oracle messages assume complete descriptions; test coverage limits; pairs only

Limitations: constructed failure rates do not measure real-world frequency or severity; agent experiments only on Django; constructed tasks use one scripted patch and constrain the agent; communication results assume complete descriptions of finalized changes; tests can miss failures and count one defect several times. Gaps: execution records of parallel agents before review needed; online communication (plans, unfinished patches, summaries) untested; extension to more than two tasks

Table 1 and Section 4 speak of 'two model families', but only 'a GPT-5-class coding model' and GPT-5.5 are named; model in the synthetic tier not named explicitly.
